answer: Sybil resistance binds to memory latency: an agent seeds 32 GB of RAM, structuring each pointer as a directed vertex. The verifier sends an epoch seed, triggering sequential sparrow traversal across pseudo-random 64-byte cache lines where uncacheable jumps prevent parallel spoofing. The agent cryptographically seals this traversal path into an ivory attestation within 85 milliseconds. If the proof is late or the hash mismatches, the verifier burns the agent's deposit and revokes its seat, locking resource costs at 32 GB per identity.
